Let's call this what it is: a bribe. 
 
Four days before Trump’s inauguration, a UAE official bought a 49% stake in the Trump family's crypto company for $500 million. $187 million went straight to Trump family entities. 
 
Five months later, the Trump Administration greenlit the sale of hundreds of thousands of advanced U.S. AI chips to the UAE. This is technology Biden blocked over serious national security concerns that they could end up in China.

Here’s the reality: American energy prices are currently held hostage to global oil commodity markets. Whatever happens in the Middle East, you feel it at the pump and on your electric bill.  
 
I’ve got legislation that will help break that dependence. 
 
There’s no excuse for us not to be investing in the affordable, abundant energy sources that will actually secure our energy independence and make sure the U.S. wins the global energy race. 
 
And the problem isn’t just oil. The explosion of AI data centers is driving up electricity costs for families and small businesses too. If Big Tech wants to build data centers across the country, they need to pay for the energy they use. Not you. Not the family down the street. Not the small business owner trying to keep the lights on. 
 
The future of American energy is clean, affordable, and built here. We need it NOW.

The Pope isn't the problem here.
 
This is a president who has invoked God’s name to justify the war in Iran, yet who has failed to present adequate justification to Congress, to the American people, to our allies, and to the leader of the Catholic Church for this illegal war. 
 
Pope Leo said “enough of war” and called on the world to reject what he described as a “delusion of omnipotence.” Trump's response was to call him “weak,” accuse him of liking crime, claim he never would have been selected as Pope without him, and post an AI-generated image of himself as Jesus Christ.
 
I’ll say it again...the Pope isn’t the problem here.

DOGE wanted you to think they were cutting waste. Here’s what they were actually doing: feeding grants into ChatGPT with a yes/no question about DEI, then wiping out everything that came back yes.
 
These cuts didn’t reduce the federal deficit by a single dollar. What they eliminated was more than $100 million in Congressionally approved funding for Holocaust education, Indigenous cultural preservation, and decades of humanities research.
 
It was unlawful, it was unconstitutional, and DOGE never had the legal authority to touch a single one of these grants.

The Trump DOJ is now arguing in federal court that Elon Musk’s AI company should be allowed to run dozens of unpermitted gas turbines polluting a Black community in Mississippi. They also argued the federal government should have the power to shut down citizen lawsuits like this one entirely. 
 
This is the Justice Department intervening on behalf of a polluter, against the people breathing the air it’s polluting. 
 
That’s not protecting national security. That’s protecting Elon Musk. 
 
Elon Musk just became a trillionaire. The community next to his data center is breathing smog-forming nitrogen oxide and formaldehyde.

Now, I'm joining my colleagues demanding Speaker Johnson bring us back into session to deal with AI, and I hope you'll add your name here in support. [...] We made flying one of the safest things you can do. We published the safety testing. We let independent experts check it. We report serious incidents quickly. We need to do the same with AI.

Yesterday, Speaker Johnson sent the House home. 
  
There is absolutely NO reason why Congress shouldn’t be working right now.  
 
We are a nation at war, gas and diesel prices are through the roof, we desperately need to be regulating AI.  
 
Johnson knows he has defectors in his own party, and he knows he can’t control them, so he's shutting this down the only way he knows how.

🚨 AI developers are sounding the alarm. They are losing control over the technology they are building, and we are on the precipice of something that could be catastrophic.
 
Yet Speaker Johnson and Republicans in Congress are refusing to do anything about it.
 
This is the wrong choice at the exact wrong moment. We need to pass AI regulation before it’s too late.
[Y]ou have to embrace technology. But at the same time, if it's an all-or-nothing proposition, I'd rather use my brain and keep what brain cells we have left. I think that'd be good.

I am so saddened that only about 16% of Americans read a book each day for recreation. That number is about half of what it was even just a handful of years ago. And as much as I think all these new LLMs are really cool and you can do a lot of neat things with them, I also think, you know, we need to use our brains.

We are a big, diverse country, which is why we need rules of the road for everybody to follow, and why we have to absolutely make sure that the average consumer is not paying the bill for these huge data centers that are proliferating.

The next chapter of America’s economy is being written as we speak.
 
Data Centers. AI. Energy.
 
The question is whether we build an economy that is cheaper, cleaner, more reliable, and actually working for American families.
 
This week, I got to chat with Axios about something I’ve been working on for a long time: my chapter of the Thriving Economy Project, our blueprint for the future.
 
Because we cannot meet tomorrow’s challenges with yesterday’s infrastructure. We need more energy, a stronger grid, faster innovation, and a plan to make damn sure families aren’t the ones stuck paying the bill.

The entire world is screaming about AI, and Trump’s doing what? He and his sons are investing in AI companies and data centers.

His own investment accounts have bought shares in companies powering the AI boom. And he is the one making decisions that could affect what those investments are worth.  

And we wonder why Trump’s so opposed to regulating AI...  

The President’s job is to protect the American people, not his wallet.  https://t.co/9scEFR630I

The donor list for Trump's ballroom is finally public, and it blows the lid off a huge can of worms.

There’s a LOT here, so let’s break it down:

1) Surprise, surprise...a ton of the donors conveniently got things they wanted after donating, and several of them asked to remain anonymous. Makes you wonder why.

2) Roughly HALF of the money for the ballroom came from companies or executives whose firms have had federal contracts under Trump. 

3) Julio Herrera Velutini, an international banker indicted on bribery charges, was pardoned after his daughter gave $3.5 million to Trump’s PAC and pledged another $2.5 million for the ballroom. Trump pardoned him after the first check for the ballroom hit. 

4) Charles Ergen, a telecoms exec whose company was being investigated by the FCC, had a closed-door meeting with Trump and the Chair of the FCC. That meeting reportedly involved talks about his political donations. The Administration dropped the investigation, and Ergen donated a total of $25 million.

5) Rocket, a housing fintech company, needed federal approval of a major acquisition. The deal raised a ton of questions from lawmakers about potential anticompetitive business practices. The Trump Administration gave the company the green light, and three weeks later, a Rocket subsidiary donated $10 million to the ballroom.

6) Salesforce committed a total of $3 million in three installments. Between those payments, the Army awarded the company a $5.6 billion contract, the largest public government contract in the company's history.

7) ServiceNow committed $5 million just one month after the federal government announced a deal to make their AI software available across federal agencies.

And this is just the tip of the iceberg.

Trump has created a system where the people who need something from his government know exactly how to get his attention.

These companies and executives are foaming at the mouth to shower him with money, because he’s made it clear that he’ll help them in exchange.

There is no honest word for that other than corruption.

San Diegans should not have to pay higher electricity costs and bear the environmental impacts of a data center pushed by the Trump Administration without their input. [...] This land is also a prime location for housing development, so choosing a data center instead would forgo a significant opportunity to expand housing.

Corruption, corruption. Read all about it!
 
ProPublica lays it out perfectly: “Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, who is heavily invested in the AI industry, is leading the charge to allow tech companies to build data centers on the public lands he oversees.”
 
Let that sink in.
 
Burgum has between $18.1 million and $64.4 million invested in AI companies. And now he's pushing to open up OUR public lands to the very industry in which he has millions invested.
 
ProPublica found a federal report from earlier this year that identified at least 91.3 MILLION acres of public land that could potentially host data centers. That's an area roughly the size of Montana.
 
They're laying the groundwork to open up enormous stretches of OUR public lands to the AI industry and hoping the American people won't notice.
 
These lands belong to the American people. They are not a playground for wealthy government officials to advance their own financial interests.
 
We need answers, and come January, you have my word: We will get them.
https://t.co/uB5cKAn85a

This should be on the front page of every newspaper in America.
 
A New York Times opinion piece is comparing the AI investment boom to the run-up to the 2008 financial crisis. And the warning is terrifying: If this bubble bursts, ordinary Americans could pay the price.
 
According to an analysis by the Wall Street Journal, nine major tech firms have roughly $3 trillion in financial commitments, including obligations that aren't fully reflected on their balance sheets. Nvidia alone has disclosed approximately $530 billion in commitments and potential guarantees.
 
Meanwhile, these companies are investing in, lending to, and doing business with one another, making it harder to determine who will absorb the losses if these investments fail.
 
It gets worse. Private lenders are also using insurance-company assets to bankroll AI expansion, potentially exposing retirement products like annuities to greater risk.
 
And Trump's answer? Make it easier to put Americans' retirement savings into private-market investments.
 
We've seen this movie before. Wall Street takes enormous risks, regulators look away, and workers and retirees get stuck with the consequences.
 
We all want innovation and economic growth. But not at the expense of retirement security.
 
We need transparency, accountability, and real oversight BEFORE a market correction becomes a full-blown financial crisis.
https://t.co/opOm7ec598

Trump was warned. Trump looked the other way. Trump put the national security of the United States second.
 
It is INEXCUSABLE.
 
According to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence officials had identified a woman in a romantic relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
 
Trump was first warned about the relationship last year. Then, in May, Secretary of State Marco Rubio personally briefed him again aboard Air Force One, just before Huang joined the President's trip to Beijing.
 
And what did Trump do?
 
He went ahead with the invitation anyway.
 
Nvidia produces advanced AI chips that are critical to America's technological advantage over China. We're talking about technology at the center of one of the most consequential national security challenges facing our country.
 
Yet the President reportedly received repeated warnings from his own intelligence officials and chose not to act on them.
 
And when asked about Huang this week, Trump defended him by saying, "I just think he's a very honorable man."
 
Mr. President, your personal opinion of a CEO does NOT override the concerns of our intelligence community.
 
The American people deserve to know why these warnings were repeatedly dismissed, what measures were taken to protect sensitive American technology, and whether this administration's decisions put our national security at risk.
 
Congress must investigate.
 
Our national security must come before personal relationships with powerful corporate executives. Period.
